## Honest analysis

**Generated against v0.7.2** (2026-10-18), relaunched after round 174's own v0.5.9 run had to be killed mid-flight to diagnose the background-repeat paint-cost bug fixed in v0.7.2 (#288). Of 500 URLs, 283 rendered on both sides, 210 failed on BOTH (almost entirely dead/moved real-world links in a corpus scraped once and not revalidated — not an engine fault), 6 failed on Chrome's side only, and exactly 1 failed on webengine's side only. Among the 283 both-rendered pages: median SSIM 0.581, median speed ratio 0.94× (essentially at parity with Chrome on the typical page; mean speed ratio 1.71× is pulled up by many small/simple pages where webengine's lower fixed overhead wins decisively).

**The real story is the tail, not the median.** A cluster of substantial, real-world, non-pathological sites render 5-50× SLOWER than Chrome and visibly wrong (low SSIM): cia.gov (85.2s vs Chrome's 2.0s, SSIM 0.088), fastly.com (67.0s, SSIM 0.125), lemonde.fr (64.6s, SSIM 0.438), www.usgs.gov (45.1s), www.cs.cmu.edu (45.1s), azure.microsoft.com (45.2s), aws.amazon.com (29.5s), gitlab.com and its blog (20-21s each), www.instructables.com (21.9s). None of these are crafted or pathological pages — they're ordinary government, cloud-platform and news sites.

Profiling cia.gov (round 176, 2026-10-21) found the single largest remaining cost was `paint.Fonts.Measure` re-shaping the same text from scratch on every call — ~25% of total CPU, with nothing between calls caching work that is naturally repeated by this engine's own layout algorithms (line-breaking, intrinsic-width estimation) and by real pages' own repeated strings (nav labels, button text). Fixed in v0.10.2 (#301) with a per-(text, family, size, weight, italic) memoization cache: Measure/Shape disappeared entirely from cia.gov's profile top-25, and total CPU for the same render dropped ~34%. **This report's own numbers predate that fix** — cia.gov and the other slow pages above should be meaningfully, but not completely, faster re-measured against v0.10.2 or later: the remaining ~45-55% of CPU (background-repeat tiling's own per-pixel compositing volume, confirmed in round 175 as inherent to how much content these pages actually paint, plus `image/draw.DrawMask`'s image-decode/resample cost) is not yet addressed.

**Worst SSIM among both-rendered pages** skews toward two distinct causes, not one: a handful of genuine content-mismatch artifacts (lego.com, baeldung.com, thingiverse.com, udemy.com course pages, all SSIM ≤0.07 — likely viewport-dependent responsive layouts or anti-bot/consent walls Chrome and webengine hit differently, not yet individually root-caused) and the already-documented slow-page cluster above, where SSIM is low because the render is simply still wrong/incomplete when the comparison runs. docs.github.com (SSIM 0.108) and lobste.rs (0.013) warrant their own look in a future round.

**Not yet re-run against current main.** A fresh full corpus run would both confirm the Measure-cache win's real-world size and surface whatever the 11 other commits that landed between v0.7.2 and v0.10.2 (SVG rasterisation rewrite, office/PDF vector output, white-space fixes, forced-synchronous-layout) changed for better or worse — queued as follow-up, not attempted in this round given a full run's multi-hour cost on a machine shared with many concurrent sessions.
